summary: Admit the bounded Russian Post batch-directory read through the existing host-mediated connector runtime.

impacts.evidence: The route resolves the connector account through the existing organization/workspace scope before using the host runtime.
The neutral projection excludes order rows and raw provider payloads; only batch identity, status, count and observation time cross the boundary.
A new provider-neutral GET route, capability and LogisticsBatchPage schema are added to the OpenAPI contract.
The read-only directory operation adds no event name, envelope or event payload.
The generated SDK surface gains listLogisticsBatches and the connector capability is admitted explicitly.
No database tables, columns, mappings or durable provider payloads are introduced.
Credentials remain callback-scoped, the provider host is fixed, query values and response fields are bounded, and malformed/duplicate data fails closed.
The operation is read-only and does not create, change or hand off a provider batch.
No durable mutation or audit record is created; the response is an ephemeral directory projection.
Repeated reads do not mutate provider state and ambiguous or oversized responses are rejected.
The host-mediated fixed-host HTTPS GET uses the existing connector egress boundary and never accepts a caller-supplied URL.
Existing host timeout, rate-limit and normalized provider-error handling covers the bounded batch read.
Removing the support capability or route disables the read without a migration or provider-side mutation.
Deterministic transport and API tests verify filters, credentials, normalization and bounded response behavior.
